verdicts.claim: CADCraft is pre-alpha; 4 of its 5 core AutoCAD workflows fail its own alpha gate (precise drafting, blocks, plotting, lossless DWG save), only dimensioning passes.
verdicts.correction: Correct, with these precisions: (1) It is the project's self-assessment, not an independent test. The upstream storytold/cadcraft ROADMAP.md (last updated 2026-10-14; still current on main as of 2026-10-21, after the v0.10.0 release) says "Stage: pre-alpha" and "four of AutoCAD's five core workflows fail the alpha gate"; docs/roadmap.md#alpha-gate (revised 2026-10-12) lists the five rows with "Works end to end?" statuses: draw/modify precisely with object snaps and tracking = "partial, blocking"; use blocks = "partial, blocking"; layers/layouts/plotting a sheet = "partial, blocking"; save DWG that AutoCAD opens without loss = "no"; dimension and annotate = "partial, not blocking" (so dimensioning "passes" the gate but is itself only partial: no DIMSTYLE dialog, MTEXT editor not in place). (2) The gate is the craftrules progress-docs core-workflow gate shared across the ArtCraft apps, applied in CADCraft's own docs; a second stated reason for pre-alpha is "ready for real work ≈ 38%", under the ~40% alpha bar; alpha is estimated ≈ 125–190 h away. (3) The ROADMAP.md banner's reasons are partly stale versus docs/roadmap.md: the banner says blocks "can't be edited in a block editor" and "plots ignore plot styles", while docs/roadmap.md (2026-10-12) records that the Block Editor (BEDIT/BSAVE/BCLOSE), xrefs, plot styles (CTB/STB), Plot dialog/preview and PUBLISH have landed, with REFEDIT, XCLIP, dynamic blocks and direct-to-printer output still missing; the row statuses and hours were explicitly left "unchanged" (still blocking). (4) Third-party coverage (e.g. pasqualepillitteri.it) merely repeats the roadmap; one mirror site reportedly labels v0.7.0 "Alpha", but that is not the project's own label. The README on main says only "Status: early development" and "Entities CADCraft doesn't model yet are not kept on save".

verdicts.claim: The never-crash policy is enforced by workspace lints (unsafe forbidden, unwrap/expect/panic denied) and 19 catch_unwind guards that restore the drawing, backed by ~40 hostile-input tests.
verdicts.correction: The never-crash policy is enforced by a workspace lint that forbids unsafe code (`[workspace.lints.rust] unsafe_code = "forbid"`; workspace clippy lints only *warn* on dbg_macro/todo) plus a crate-root attribute `#![deny(clippy::unwrap_used, clippy::expect_used, clippy::panic, clippy::unimplemented, clippy::todo, clippy::unreachable)]` carried by all 15 production crate roots (12 crates + 3 apps) — the unwrap/expect/panic denial is per-crate, not a workspace lint. There are 20 `catch_unwind` call sites in non-test code (21 if a test-only one in apps/cadcraft/src/logging.rs is counted) across 8 files, but only the engine command paths restore the drawing: `Session::execute` (crates/engine/src/lib.rs:896) and the LISP runner (crates/engine/src/lisp/mod.rs:313) snapshot and restore doc+selection, and interactive `begin`/`input` (guard.rs, lib.rs:1231) end the command with an internal error so the session restores it. The other guards (guard.rs prompt/preview/drag/editing_mtext, 4 in crates/dwg, 1 in crates/fonts, 1 in crates/ui-egui canvas rebuild, 2 around file open) only convert a panic into an error or fallback. Hostile-input regression tests number ~101 test functions workspace-wide (40 in the engine crate alone, 26 in io, 11 render, 8 doc, 5 fonts, 4 geom, 2 constraints, 2 dxf, 1 ui-egui, 2 apps), of which 49 have never_panic/does_not_panic in the name; "~40" matches only the engine crate.

verdicts.claim: An xref is a Block with xref_path saved exactly as given; its objects are loaded from the referenced file's model space at open and on Reload and never saved with the host; xref_status is session-only
verdicts.correction: Correct, with these precisions: (1) The path is stored verbatim (only trimmed of surrounding whitespace by `-xref path`) in `Block::xref_path` and written unchanged into the BLOCK record's group 1 (flag 4, plus 8 for an overlay); the DXF reader stores group 1 verbatim and ignores any entities inside a BLOCK flagged 4. (2) Objects are the referenced drawing's model space (`x.model`, adopted with fresh handles, references renamed to `xref|name`, dimension associativity cleared; its INSBASE/INSUNITS become the block's base/units; its blocks come along as `xref|name`). They are loaded not only at OPEN (`after_open` -> `load_all`) and `-xref Reload`, but also at XATTACH, `-xref Attach/Overlay` and `-xref Path`. (3) 'Never saved' holds for both DXF and DWG: `saved_view` empties every block that has an `xref_path` and is applied inside `tags_for`, which both the DXF writer (`tags`) and the DWG bridge (`dwg_bridge`) use. (4) `xref_status` is never written to DXF/DWG (neither format has a field for it; `mark_xrefs` writes only flags and path), reads back as the default `NotLoaded`, and is recomputed by `after_open`, so an Unloaded xref is reloaded on reopen (docs/gaps.md F2: 'Unloaded state and xref-layer overrides last only for the session'). Strictly, the field is `#[serde(default)]` rather than `#[serde(skip)]`, so a serde serialization of `Block` would include it; 'session-only' means 'not persisted in any drawing file', not 'excluded from serde'.

verdicts.claim: Stored paths are followed only on this computer or the drawing's own network share; UNC paths to other hosts, file://host URLs, device paths and URL schemes are refused with a reason and treated like a missing file
verdicts.correction: The claim is correct in substance; precise wording: Paths stored in a drawing (xref paths and table data links) are resolved only through craft_docpath (pinned at craft-libs rev 82a24b0 in /home/user/cadcraft_1/Cargo.toml), a lexical, no-I/O check. A relative stored path is taken from the drawing's folder; a UNC path is followed only when its host and share equal the drawing's own share (compared ignoring ASCII case), otherwise it is refused as Refused::Network ("the path is on another computer"). file: URLs with a non-local host (anything but an empty host or "localhost") are refused as Network, while file:///path, file://localhost/path and file:///C:/... are accepted as local paths. Device paths (\\.\, \\?\ non-drive, \??\, and DOS reserved names such as CON, NUL, COM1 with or without extension) are refused as Refused::Device ("the path names a device, not a file"); non-file URL schemes (http, https, smb, webdav, mailto, data, javascript, ms-word, ...) are refused as Refused::Url ("the link is not a file path"); empty/control-character/above-root paths, and relative paths when the drawing has no file, are Refused::Invalid. Consequences: an xref with a refused path is not loaded, its block stays empty, and its status is XrefStatus::Unresolved (not NotFound) with the log line "<path>: not opened, <reason>"; -XREF ? shows no foundAt, XOPEN fails with the reason, and reload follows the saved path the same way. As with a genuinely missing file, the loader still looks for a file of the same name beside the host drawing, so a same-named local copy can satisfy a refused xref path. A refused table data link is reported as a per-link error "<path>: not opened, <reason>" and nothing is read (no fallback). Paths the user types (XATTACH, -XREF Path, DATALINK) are used as given. The behaviour is documented only in code comments and the craft-libs README; no cadcraft docs/ page mentions it, and the craftrules standards repo could not be checked (not accessible from this session).

verdicts.claim: Vertical alignments and corridors exist in BricsCAD civil tools and require projection; horizontal alignments import from LandXML and Civil 3D

Precise wording: In BricsCAD Pro's Civil tools, vertical alignments (built by placing PVIs on the TIN-surface profile under a horizontal alignment, viewed with ALIGNMENTVIEW) and corridors (CORRIDOR command: a corridor template swept along a 3D alignment or string, or a 'simple corridor' along horizontal-alignment PI points on a TIN surface) both exist, and both require the horizontal alignment to first be projected (draped) onto a TIN surface ("Projection is required to create Vertical Alignments and Corridors"). Alignments can be imported two ways: LANDXMLIMPORT brings in Horizontal Alignments (by PI and by Elements), 3D Alignments, TIN surfaces, civil points and strings, and imported LandXML vertical alignments automatically create 3D Alignments; CIVIL3DIMPORT reads a Civil 3D DWG (or converts the current drawing) and imports Alignments (by PI and by Elements) AND Profiles (vertical alignments), plus COGO points, point groups, TIN/volume/grid surfaces and profile views. So it is not only horizontal alignments that import; vertical alignments/profiles do too. Minor caveats: LANDXMLIMPORT is documented as not available on Linux, and corridors themselves are not imported (they are rebuilt in BricsCAD from a template plus 3D alignment).

Precise wording: In a January 2025 Bricsys forum thread ("Panning and crashing"), a user running BricsCAD V25.1.07-1 (Civil/survey workflow, small drawing of survey points, linework and a few blocks) reported a fatal error while panning or zooming. verdicts.claim: PVWatts v8 accepts albedo, bifaciality, soiling, gcr and dc_ac_ratio inputs
verdicts.correction: Correct, with these precisions: all five are optional request parameters of the PVWatts v8 API (GET /api/pvwatts/v8). dc_ac_ratio: decimal, default 1.2, must be positive. gcr: decimal, default 0.4, range 0.01-0.99. bifaciality: decimal, range 0-1, no default (ratio of rear- to front-side efficiency; typically 0.65-0.9). albedo: a single decimal or a pipe-delimited array of 12 monthly values, each >0 and <1, no default (a companion flag use_wf_albedo=0/1 selects weather-file albedo instead). soiling: a pipe-delimited array of 12 monthly values in percent, range 0-100, no default (new in v8 as the "monthly irradiance losses" input; bifaciality/albedo are also new relative to v6). Note the underlying SSC pvwattsv8 compute module has different internal defaults (dc_ac_ratio 1.1, gcr 0.3) than the web API's documented defaults (1.2, 0.4).

verdicts.claim: 2010 ADA Standards Table 208.2 scopes accessible spaces by lot size and one in six accessible spaces must be van-accessible
verdicts.correction: Correct in substance, imprecise in wording. Precise version: 2010 ADA Standards section 208.2 / Table 208.2 ("Parking Spaces") sets the minimum number of accessible spaces based on the "Total Number of Parking Spaces Provided in Parking Facility" -- i.e. the count of spaces (not physical lot area), calculated separately for each parking facility (lot or structure), not on the site-wide total. Rows: 1-25 -> 1; 26-50 -> 2; 51-75 -> 3; 76-100 -> 4; 101-150 -> 5; 151-200 -> 6; 201-300 -> 7; 301-400 -> 8; 401-500 -> 9; 501-1000 -> 2 percent of total; 1001 and over -> 20 plus 1 for each 100, or fraction thereof, over 1000 (separate percentages apply to hospital outpatient 10%, rehab/outpatient PT 20%, and residential facilities under 208.2.1-208.2.3). Section 208.2.4 Van Parking Spaces: "For every six or fraction of six parking spaces required by 208.2 to comply with 502, at least one shall be a van parking space complying with 502" -- so the 1-in-6 ratio counts required accessible spaces (not total spaces), rounds up ("or fraction of six"), and always yields at least one van space. Note: DOJ's restriping brief table reads "500 to 1000" where the Standards say "501 to 1000".

verdicts.claim: eTransmit does not automatically include SHX/TTF fonts, .pat, .lin, .pmp, OLE links or URL-referenced files.
verdicts.correction: Correct, with two precisions. (1) The cited "Transmittal Package File Reference" (AutoCAD 2027) lists under "File Types Not Added Automatically": *.shx, *.ttf, *.pfa/*.pfb (PostScript Type 1 fonts), *.pat, *.lin, *.pmp, and "OLE objects (linked files)". It does not mention URL-referenced files; that part comes from a different Autodesk page, the Files Tree / Files Table tab reference for the Create Transmittal dialog: "Related files that are referenced by URLs are not included in the transmittal package." (2) Fonts are a default-off option rather than impossible to include: the Standard transmittal setup omits them, but the Modify Transmittal Setup dialog's "Include Fonts" checkbox adds TTF and SHX files to the package (Autodesk KB: "The default transmittal configuration does not include fonts"). By contrast .pat, .lin, .pmp, linked OLE files and URL-referenced files have no include option and must be added manually via Add File. Note the asymmetry on plotter files: PC3 (and CTB/STB) ARE added automatically; only the companion PMP is not. A precise wording: "By default (Standard setup) eTransmit does not include SHX, TTF or PostScript fonts (these can be added with the Include Fonts option), and it never automatically adds .pat, .lin, .pmp, linked OLE files, or files referenced by URL."
